title: This week
body:
Softmax Implementation

- Changed the external interface to signed INT8 scores and probability codes 0–127, supporting 1–196 values per row. Uses a 256 × 16-bit exponential LUT and 23-cycle unsigned restoring division.
- Passed 9 software tests and bit-exact RTL checks on 578 rows / 25,999 outputs. Standalone routed timing passed 90 MHz using 175 ALMs, 3 M10Ks and 0 DSPs (setup slack +3.894 ns).
- On 10 images, probability relative RMSE was 6.634% and attention-context (P@V) relative RMSE was 2.532%. Independent INT8 rounding does not enforce row sums of 1; 196-key model accuracy still needs validation.
- Next: resolve scale/layout interfaces and integrate with matmul and the full SoC. Board operation and end-to-end speedup have not been tested.

LayerNorm Implementation and Timing

- Built signed INT8 input/output LayerNorm for 1–576 channels, with INT8 gamma/beta supplied per row. Uses a 25-cycle digit-by-digit integer square root and 41-cycle restoring division; internal normalization retains 14 fractional bits.
- Calibrated scales on 7 images and checked 3 held-out images: validation relative RMSE was 3.485%, with 0.0961% input clipping. Top-1 predictions matched on 10 isolated replacement tests; this is not a dataset accuracy result.
- Passed 9 software tests and bit-exact RTL checks on 744 rows / 200,296 outputs. Pipelining and proven width reductions preserved integer results and closed standalone 90 MHz timing: 510 ALMs, 4 M10Ks and 8 DSPs (setup slack +0.321 ns).
- Next: validate more model sites, channel ordering and parameter/scaling interfaces, then integrate, recheck full-SoC timing and test on the board.
